findings.title: Reserved role codes can grant tenant-wide operating scope outside the permission grant ceiling
findings.review: independently source-reviewed by audit_roadmap_review; native characterization execution owned by root

runtimeEvidence.outcome: 23 passed / 1 failed at final expected LOCATIONS, received TENANT assertion; harness exit 1; securityQualificationPassed:false
runtimeEvidence.isolation: dedicated local PostgreSQL database; real guards/role/member/operating-scope services; Better Auth transport and Next headers stubbed; cluster stopped; source hashes unchanged
runtimeEvidence.limit: Confirms native service composition and actual unexpected scope, not full signed-cookie HTTP action invocation or proof of downstream data exfiltration

relatedUnqualifiedPaths: access-request role approval/application reuse member policy
findings.trigger: A current narrow role manager holds roles.create, roles.permissions.assign, users.read, users.roles.assign and dashboard.read, but lacks tenant-wide operating authority. An unused Admin or Super Admin display name is created with only dashboard.read and then granted to a separate active tenant member.
findings.sourceMechanism: createRoleName turns display name into admin/super_admin. saveRole/checkPermissionChanges and canGrantMemberRole inspect permission arrays, not code-derived authority. resolveTenantWideOperatingAuthority treats those role codes as TENANT_WIDE; owner and manager server paths consume that decision.
findings.impact: Same-tenant location/operating scope expansion (not cross-tenant escape). Existing administrator code collision can block that particular name but unused admin/super_admin alternatives remain.
preconditions: Fresh actor session with assuranceVerifiedAt within 300s and matching organization
Unused reserved code in same tenant
Role/member request UUIDs and fresh memberAccessRevision after creation
Target session/context obtained again after assignment revokes target sessions
Relevant dashboard module admitted for end-to-end action read

repairPackage.scope: Review code-derived authority as an explicit capability; stop arbitrary names from minting privileged operating scope; ensure all grant paths enforce scope ceiling and inventory existing custom reserved-code roles before any data remediation.
acceptance: Narrow role creator/assigner cannot produce or delegate broader operating scope through any reserved-code spelling
Legitimate owner/admin provisioning retains intended scope by reviewed trusted policy
Existing custom reserved-code records are explicitly classified, not silently deleted/revoked
Native create+assign+fresh-context test shows no scope expansion; owner/manager negative reads return no disallowed location data
repairPackage.rollback: No migration/production flag change in this package; retain prior policy artifact and inventory; do not restore exploitable scope policy as an automatic rollback after admission.
repairPackage.gate: Blocks operating-access/owner/manager production qualification until repaired and independently verified

findings.title: Item action error responses expose arbitrary exception text

runtimeEvidence.outcome: 4 characterization cases passed, reproducing sentinel disclosure through 2 actual read handlers on guard and service exceptions
runtimeEvidence.isolation: all imported authority/service/schema/cache/error dependencies explicitly mocked; no real DB/network
runtimeEvidence.limit: Synthetic injected error, not live private/DB payload; 7 additional mutation catches are source-only, not exercised by these 4 tests

findings.trigger: A guard or service rejects with an Error containing internal details; catch returns error.message directly to the action caller.
findings.impact: Arbitrary supplied exception text reaches failed client response; actual live confidential/DB payload is not established by source-only review or synthetic injection.

repairPackage.scope: Normalize error responses in this single actions/item/items.ts family using existing safe action helper. Keep explicit nonprivate not-found/business outcomes. Do not alter transaction logic.
acceptance: Synthetic private sentinel absent from all failed responses for authorization and service exceptions
Denied guard never invokes item read/write service
Preserve successful response DTOs and explicit fixed Item not found result
Before-repair characterization is 4/4 reproduced; post-repair acceptance must assert sentinel absence, not presence.
repairPackage.rollback: Revert only owned response-normalization hunks if regression; keep vulnerable endpoints outside production admission until corrected.
repairPackage.gate: Blocks private-error response qualification for the affected entrypoints
